taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes S. tristichus was formerly lumped in S. undulatus and that precise boundaries with S. consobrinus and S. cowlesi remain unresolved; Colorado Parks and Wildlife still presents prairie lizard and plateau fence lizard on one page.
fieldMarks: Spiny lizard: keeled, pointed scales on the upper side and keeled, overlapping scales on the rear of the thigh.
Colour extremely variable, usually striped or crossbanded.
Adult males have blue patches on the sides of the throat and belly, in Colorado mountain populations with a wide black margin.
Adult males show two enlarged scales on the underside of the tail base behind the vent and two bulges from the hemipenes.
Total length up to about 19 cm (7.5 in); Colorado Parks and Wildlife describes it as slightly spinier than the prairie lizard.
behavior: Diurnal basker: inactive in cold spells and in the hottest part of a summer day, using sunny open spots in cool weather and shade when hot.
Active roughly May to early October in Wyoming; females lay one to three clutches of 4-17 eggs in June or July and hatchlings appear in August.
Insectivore: flies, grasshoppers, crickets, leafhoppers, ants, moths, plus spiders, ticks, millipedes and snails.
Perches on rocks but also uses trees, logs, debris piles, buildings and dirt banks.
habitat: Open, rocky or shrubby ground: sunny rock outcrops, boulders, sandstone cliffs, hogbacks and canyon walls in sagebrush and shrubland, sometimes near abandoned buildings.
NatureServe lists openly wooded, shrubby or rocky areas.
range: Southwestern Wyoming, eastern and southern Utah, western and south-central Colorado, northern and central Arizona and northern New Mexico; not in Canada. In Wyoming it is confined to the lower Green River valley and a narrow strip at the east edge of the Laramie Mountains.

lookalikes.name: Prairie lizard (Sceloporus consobrinus)
lookalikes.howToTell: Near-identical in the hand; Colorado Parks and Wildlife says the plateau fence lizard looks slightly spinier, and they are separated mainly by range.

lookalikes.name: Southwestern fence lizard (Sceloporus cowlesi)
lookalikes.howToTell: Separated by range (eastern Arizona and central New Mexico southward); the two hybridize in an ecotone in eastern Arizona.

aliases: Red-lipped plateau lizard (former subspecies S. undulatus erythrocheilus in Wyoming)
Northern plateau lizard (former subspecies S. undulatus elongatus in Wyoming)
